I feel like I can’t sit still, even when I’m exhausted. If I’m editing photos, I’m bouncing my leg, getting up, pacing around the apartment, starting the dishes in the middle of culling a gallery, then forgetting what I was doing.

Quiet time is almost impossible. I’ll put on a movie with my husband or try to read, and within minutes I’m talking over it, grabbing my phone, rearranging shelves. When I’m shooting weddings, I catch myself blurting things out before people finish their sentences, cutting off the planner or the bride with my own ideas. I’ll jump into conversations that aren’t really mine, like I can’t wait my turn.

Inside, it feels like this restless buzz—like I should be doing three things at once. Sometimes I’ll suddenly take on extra shoots or start some big project at 2 a.m., convinced it’s a great idea, and then a few days later I crash and wonder what I was thinking. I can’t tell if this is just my personality or something else.
D003-D008_h001.question_a:

I’d blurt things out, cut people off mid‑sentence, or wander around the classroom when everyone else was sitting. It never really went away; it just looks different now.

At weddings, I’m constantly on the move. Even during breaks, I can’t just sit and relax with the other vendors. I’m pacing, checking things, jumping into conversations and talking over people without meaning to. My mind and body feel like they’re on fast‑forward all day, every day, whether it’s a big event or just a night at home with my husband.

Sometimes my mood gets noticeably “up”—I’ll feel extra chatty, more confident, sleep a bit less for a few days—but the fidgety, restless, intrusive stuff is there even when my mood is normal or low. It doesn’t switch on and off with those mood changes; it’s just a constant background hum I can’t turn down.

At shoots, I’ll interrupt clients’ conversations to suggest poses or new locations, almost barging in without thinking if it’s appropriate.

It’s been on and off for… I don’t know, maybe a couple of years, but the past few months it’s really getting in my way.

On my shift, I’m supposed to stay on the platform section they assign me, but I keep pacing up and down the whole time. I’ll start wiping seats, then I have to move, so I leave the cart and walk to the other end, then remember I left the cart behind. I can’t sit still on my breaks either; I’ll get up, wander around the station, sometimes even go outside for no real reason.

My mind feels jumpy. When my supervisor is explaining what area I’m supposed to cover, I drift off halfway through. I lose track of what she said and have to ask again. At home, I start laundry, then notice the dishes, then go to check my phone—everything half-done, nothing actually finished. Making a simple list for groceries or bills turns into a mess; I lay things out, then forget where I put the paper.

People say I cut them off a lot. I don’t mean to, but as soon as something pops into my head, I blurt it out. Even with my coworkers, I jump into their tasks or conversations without really being asked, like I can’t hold myself back.
D003-D008_h021.question_a:
I’ve always been this way, even as a kid. My teachers used to tell my mom I could never stay in my seat, always fidgeting, getting up to “help” when nobody asked. I still feel like that now—like my body’s revving all the time. On the train at work, even on my break, I’ll get up and walk the platform instead of sitting, like I can’t stand being still. I rush through cleaning one car, then jump to the next before I’ve finished properly.

I cut people off a lot without meaning to—coworkers, my sister on the phone—my words just come out before I’ve really listened. At staff meetings I’ll blurt stuff out, then realize someone else was talking. I start tasks at home—laundry, bills, cooking—and half the time I jump to something else and forget what I was doing. My apartment’s a mess because I can’t seem to keep things in order.

Some nights, especially around the anniversary of my husband’s death, my mood gets really low, and other times I feel more upbeat and talkative, but this constant restlessness and impulsiveness is there all the time, no matter how my mood is.
D003-D008_h021.question_b:

I’ve been a janitor in the same office building for years, but the last few months my wife says I’m “all over the place.” I can’t seem to stay put. Even during the tenants’ meetings, when I’m supposed to sit in the back quietly, I’m up and down, pacing in the hallway, checking doors that don’t really need checking. I feel this sort of buzz inside, like I’ve got to keep moving.

When I’m talking with people, I catch myself cutting them off, finishing their sentences, jumping in with my own ideas before they’re done. It happens with my boss, with my grandkids, even at church. I don’t mean to be rude; it’s like I can’t wait my turn.

At work I start one task, like mopping a floor, then halfway through I remember something else and wander off. I lose track of what I was doing. My closet is a mess—supplies everywhere—because I can’t seem to plan out what I’m doing or stick to a system.

Some days this restless energy is stronger than others, but I can’t really say if it’s tied to my mood or just…me getting worse with age.
D003-D008_h024.question_a:
I’ve always been kind of wound up, even as a kid. Teachers used to send notes home because I couldn’t stay in my seat and was always blurting things out or cutting people off. My mom said I was “go, go, go” from the minute I woke up. That’s never really gone away.

At work now, I’m supposed to sit through safety meetings, but I can’t stay put. I’ll get up, pace in the back, or find some excuse to step out. My legs feel jumpy, like I’ve got to keep moving. Even on my days off, my wife says I can’t just sit and watch a movie—I’m up changing lightbulbs, checking the basement, anything.

I have a hard time sticking with one task. I’ll start cleaning one floor, then something catches my eye and I wander off to another job, and I forget to finish the first one. Keeping my supplies and schedule straight is a mess; I lose track of what I was doing all the time.

Sometimes my mood lifts and I feel unusually upbeat or irritable for a few days, but this restlessness and butting into people’s conversations is there whether my mood is up, down, or just normal.
D003-D008_h024.question_b:

At work on the night shift, I just cannot stay still. I’m supposed to be watching the monitors or doing my rounds calmly, but I keep popping up out of my chair, pacing the halls, starting little projects I don’t finish. My body feels like it’s buzzing, like I’m being pushed from the inside. I rush from one floor to another, cleaning, fixing things no one asked me to, talking to whoever’s around and cutting them off mid-sentence because my thoughts are racing and I need to get them out. My wife complains that at home I can’t sit through a whole TV show or a meal; I keep jumping up, wandering around, starting tasks and then abandoning them for something else that suddenly seems more important.
